items.headline: Wall Street Reeled as AI Stock Sell-Off Triggered Broad Market Decline
items.summary: U.S. equities experienced a brutal sell-off today, largely driven by a sharp decline in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks amidst concerns over potential new regulations and a slowdown in data center expansion. The major indices erased previous day's gains, with the Nasdaq entering correction territory. Market sentiment was broadly negative, with investors seeking safer assets like Treasury bonds.

items.headline: S&P 500 Performance
items.statContext: Closed -4.4% (-334.89 points) today, marking its worst day since April 2025.

items.headline: NASDAQ Composite Performance
items.statContext: Closed -5.5% (-1,421.52 points) today, entering correction territory at 11.9% below its October high.

items.headline: MNTN, Inc. Plunges on Weakened Guidance
items.summary: MNTN, Inc. ($MNTN) shares plummeted 55.11% to close at $5.97, after the company cut its 2026 revenue forecast and announced a new chief executive.

items.headline: NVIDIA Leads Chip Sector Declines
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) fell 9.26% to $181.60 as the leading chipmaker continued to feel the brunt of the AI stock sell-off, driven by concerns over potential data center regulations.

items.headline: AMD Tumbles Amid AI Sell-Off
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) tumbled 15.5% as the broader sell-off in AI and chip stocks intensified following midterm election results and data center regulation fears.

items.headline: Antelope Enterprise Holdings Surges
items.summary: Antelope Enterprise Holdings ($AEHL) was a notable gainer, soaring 111.3% to $13.25 by midday, although specific drivers for the surge were not immediately clear.

items.headline: AppLovin Jumps on Strong Earnings and Buyback
items.summary: AppLovin ($LOV) shares jumped 28.5% after the marketing platform reported stronger-than-expected revenue and profit, and approved a new stock buyback program valued at $3.2 billion.

items.headline: AI and Tech Sectors Lead Market Decline
items.summary: Information Technology was the worst-performing sector, falling 7.30%, as concerns grew over potential slowdowns in AI infrastructure build-out following the U.S. midterm elections and fears of new regulations. Consumer Staples, despite a 0.67% loss, was the best-performing sector for the day.

items.headline: Fed Signals Potential December Rate Hike Amid Inflation Concerns
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained current interest rates at its October meeting but signaled potential rate increases in December due to persistent inflation. Recent forecasts indicate a reacceleration of inflation, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) projected to rise to 4.25% and Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) to 4.03% in November.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data Released
items.summary: Encouraging reports showed fewer U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week, and nonfarm productivity improved more than expected during the summer. The U.S. Census Bureau also released new data products from its Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS). U.S. GDP grew at an annualized 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports for November 5, 2026
items.summary: Cummins ($CMI) reported strong quarterly revenue but reduced its full-year forecast due to weaker demand for pickup truck engines, leading to a 4.31% drop. Toyota ($TM) and ConocoPhillips ($COP) saw gains following their earnings releases. Several tech companies, including SoundHound AI ($SOUN), IREN ($IREN), and IonQ ($IONQ), are scheduled to report after market close. Oscar Health ($OSCR), Cigna Group ($CI), and Primo Brands ($PRMB) also reported positive Q3 results.

items.headline: AI Regulation Fears and Oil Price Fluctuations Impact Markets
items.summary: Democratic midterm election victories have sparked investor fears of potential regulations slowing the AI data center build-out, especially in Texas, contributing heavily to the tech sector's decline. Meanwhile, Brent crude oil rose 3.9% today, recovering some losses, but uncertainty persists regarding the ongoing conflict in Iran. Treasury yields continued to ease, signaling a flight to safety among investors.
